piece: W1-19 — the main quest, end to end
note: This file carries no `quests` array on purpose, so QuestBook skips it. The quests are in mainline-act1..act5.json and mainline-backpath.json. This is the registry the mainline's own metrics are computed against, and RI-WLD09 §B3's `unanswered[]` lives here because RI-WLD09 names game/data/quests/mainline.json by path.
title: The Rootward Tide
premise: Deaths are not arriving at the roots. The Drowned Court of Soulrest has it as a curve in a four-hundred-year burial ledger rather than as a rumour, and it hires an outlander to carry its books because an outlander owes no root anything.
authorial_truth: RI-LOR05 §6 cause C, registered as CF-C010 with authorially_true: true. A pre-Duskfall xanmeer reservoir under the Stone Wastes near Soulrest was built to hold souls and never stopped. The sapwells of the province work because of the allowance it lets past. Causes A (soul-gem interception on the coast) and B (thirty years of sapwell cutting) are real, criminal, growing, and demonstrably insufficient, and the player who acts on either does genuine good and fixes nothing.

handler.role: The Drowned Court's Undersexton at Soulrest. Runs the player as an asset, pays in gold, tells the truth about facts and not about purposes.

antagonist.title: the Steward of the Count
antagonist.present_from: Act I quest 2, as a sound under the Stone Wastes at night and eleven burial boxes that came back the weight of nothing
antagonist.named_at: Act II quest 1 (Q-MAIN-06 journal 55), in the fourth volume of the Drowned Tally, in the margins he has been correcting for three hundred years
antagonist.own_words_at: Act II quest 5 (Q-MAIN-10 journal 40), a letter of instruction taken off a body in the Deep Marshes eleven years ago

verified_claims.claim: The curve is older than the cutting.
verified_claims.verified_by: Q-MAIN-06 res_the_number / res_the_fair_copy — the player added up four hundred years of the Drowned Tally themselves and found the deficit begins eight years before the first cutting licence.

verified_claims.claim: The wells drink what the machine lets past; stopping it stops them.
verified_claims.verified_by: Q-MAIN-12 — the player closed the sixth intake with their own hand and watched the Soulrest well go cold, or derived it from Ivo Sarn's flows.

verified_claims.claim: The soul-gem trade cannot account for the curve.
verified_claims.verified_by: Q-MAIN-08 — the player counted the true tonnage out of Archon and it is five times what it was and nothing against four hundred years of return column.

antagonist.refutation_audit: No authored voice anywhere in this piece asserts that Ixtu-Meer was simply wrong. Checked across: all 32 quests' journal entries, all resolution outcomes, all ending world flags, the aftermath quest, and game/data/dialogue/topics/main-quest-argument.json. The only answer the game gives his case is the player's action, and three of the five endings leave his case standing.

mandate.name: the ninth clause of the Ninth Recension of the Drowned Tally
mandate.text: When the tide fails, the count will be read by one who is owed nothing — not of the marsh, not of the Court, and holding no debt to any root.
mandate.adjudication_audit: No quest, book, NPC line or ending in this piece states whether the ninth clause is genuine. Q-MAIN-05 offers the ink evidence and the older recension that cancels it; Q-MAIN-09 offers Bel Mourne's eleven-year argument and the archivist's thirty-year refusal to answer; Q-MAIN-26 offers the antagonist saying only that he never wrote in the Recension, which settles nothing; Q-MAIN-30 establishes that the Court has severed three claimants in four hundred years and carried on, which is not evidence either way. Every ending sets the_recension_is_still_unsettled.

backpath.warned_at: Q-MAIN-29 journal 30, in the player's own voice, before the third root is cut

point_of_no_return.position_note: 27 of the 28 acted mainline quests sit behind it. RI-EXP05 LH2 bar is >= 0.94.
point_of_no_return.modal_note: There is no confirmation dialog, no 'you cannot return' string, no autosave prompt and no UI surface of any kind. The crossing is a resolution whose method is `wait` and whose journal entry is one sentence about a stone.

signal_channels.where: Q-MAIN-27 journal 20, and she says it at the Bone Ladder well in Q-MAIN-25 three weeks of simulated time earlier, as an ordinary fact about her job
the player works it out themselves from a keeper's remark and a dockmaster paying people off, and writes that down

Q-MAIN-27 journal 24 and 28 — barges moved to the deep-water berth, work stopped on the twelfth root, the sick-tent struck, thirty of sixty hands paid off, the Court's chapter sitting four days over what happens to the road

closes.in_fiction: the sextons say the chapter closed it behind you and will not sit again this season
the working parts will not take a hand from the gallery once the floor has your weight — Ei-Vashan said so at the well
the camp broke up; Weeja-Sen paid her hands and they went home

closes.thread: unfinished business with the eight voices
closes.in_fiction: each of the eight says, in their own words, that the thing they were owed is now moot

endings.wells: re-issue province-wide but degraded; tithe-gourd carries fewer charges, permanently, for everyone
unchanged; the crisis is managed at a rate the player sets and the player does not come up
unchanged for now; the allowance drifts with nobody at the ledger
unchanged; nothing anywhere is different and the journal records it as a decision
dead province-wide, permanently; the tithe is taken and nothing is given back; the doomed world persists
half-restored over a season with six intakes dead and the allowance drifting

unanswered.question: Is the ninth clause of the Ninth Recension genuine, or was it written for the Court by somebody who needed a claimant?
unanswered.refused_or_evaded: Rell answers that what she believes is not the useful question. Hosk-Vei answers that the Court has been arguing it for four hundred years and nobody has ever won it. Neither answers the question.

unanswered.question: What was the reservoir under the Stone Wastes built to do — hold souls in reverence to Sithis, or in fear of it?
unanswered.book_note: Two in-world texts give incompatible accounts and neither is corroborated. This is the one question RI-WLD09 §B3 permits to be answered in a book and not in dialogue, and it is answered by two books that disagree, which is evidence and not an answer.

unanswered.question: Whose count is being kept on the player?
unanswered.note: RI-WLD09 §B3 requires at least one unanswered question asked by the antagonist about the player rather than by the player about the world. This is it, and nothing in the game answers it.

unanswered.question: Why did the tree at Thorn ask for the player, and why did it stop at four sentences?
unanswered.asked_of: the Hist of Thorn, three times, in three different ways (Q-MAIN-15 journal 50)
unanswered.refused_or_evaded: It did not answer and it did not go away.

unanswered.question: Who told the Blackwood Company what was under the Stone Wastes, and what happened to two of the eleven Lilmoth hands who went into the rotting quarter?
unanswered.raised_at: Q-MAIN-19 journal 34, Q-MAIN-21 journal 30, Q-MAIN-24 journal 92
unanswered.asked_of: the Company's factor, in the player's own sick-tent, with a broken leg (Q-MAIN-24 journal 92)
unanswered.refused_or_evaded: He gives an account of who told him and the player writes down that they do not believe the second half of it. No other source corroborates or contradicts it.

faction_independence.note: No quest in the mainline sets rank_gate. Faction rank appears only in resolutions[].requires.faction_rank, on six of the eight Act IV quests, always alongside at least two routes that require no standing at all. Q-MAIN-04 res_no_name is a first-class win that takes no name anywhere and sets act_iv_leverage_must_be_bought, which is a price and not a wall.

declared_incomplete_note: Wave 1. The quests are complete and completable end to end; what is thin is depth — the Act V conversation has its twelve topics but the twelve topic bodies are one exchange each, the aftermath's nine disagreeing accounts are six, and the intake keepers on the counting floor are eleven ids with three distinct bodies of text between them. RI-EXP05 §D LH11's specificity resolver and LH12's forty-NPC sweep are named by that item and are not built by this piece.
